verdictSummary: The visible AI copywriting loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. ClosersCopy earns its keep through model, data, workflow, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private AI copywriting workspace that sends user text to one chosen model, stores versions, applies reusable instructions, and exports Markdown.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: ClosersCopy: Customers pay for tuned workflows, predictable quality, governance, and a product team absorbing model churn rather than for the text box alone.
ongoingBurden: Maintain prompts, model migrations, cost controls, evaluations, privacy, and failure handling.

priorArt.name: Ollama
priorArt.desc: Local model runner for private text-generation workflows.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Open-source interface and workflow layer for local or hosted language models.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A local-first AI desk with reusable agents, documents, memory, and workflows; less campaign theatre, more settings.

facts.install: Desktop installer for macOS/Windows/Linux, or Docker for a self-hosted web instance
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp models plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and many cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter and Mistral
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local storage; self-hosted data is stored in the mounted server storage and chosen vector database (LanceDB by default), while prompts sent to cloud models leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can run custom sales-copy prompts, but it lacks ClosersCopy's dedicated frameworks, long-form editor, and guided sales-copy workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful results still require downloading a local model or supplying a model-provider API key

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted AI workbench with saved prompts, knowledge, web search, and multi-model comparison; powerful, not especially house-trained.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image, install the Python package, or deploy with Kubernetes
facts.engines: Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API, including LM Studio, vLLM, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter; additional speech, image and search providers
facts.dataFormat: By default, chats and account data live in a local SQLite webui.db, uploads in a data/uploads directory and embeddings in the configured vector store; PostgreSQL and object storage are optional
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a general AI workbench rather than a purpose-built sales-copy environment with framework management and a specialized long-form editor.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must install Docker or a compatible Python environment, mount persistent storage correctly, and separately provide Ollama or an API endpoint

alternatives.name: Witsy
alternatives.desc: System-wide selected-text commands, reusable experts, a scratchpad, and document context; bring the model and skip the subscription.

facts.install: Download a desktop binary from GitHub Releases; macOS also supports `brew install --cask witsy`
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, Meta, Ollama, LM Studio, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, Azure and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus optional image, video, speech, search and MCP providers
facts.dataFormat: Conversation history, experts, settings and document repositories live in the local application profile; local files are indexed locally, while prompts and retrieved context sent to a cloud model leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: Its experts and text commands can execute copy frameworks, but it does not provide ClosersCopy's dedicated campaign canvas, scoring, or guided long-form process.
facts.setupBlocker: It is BYOK unless you install Ollama and a local model; system-wide commands also need OS accessibility permissions

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of ClosersCopy is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for ClosersCopy, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private AI copywriting workspace that sends user text to one chosen model, stores versions, applies reusable instructions, and exports Markdown.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: team governance and integrations; vendor-managed prompt and quality tuning; proprietary models or classifiers.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
